response_json.request: Add cylindrical heads on the long pins to prevent link arms against slipping off.

actions.relational_constraint: The cylindrical heads must be positioned coaxially on both exposed axial ends of each of the four long corner pivot pins. Each head must have a diameter greater than the 4.8 mm pin shaft and the 5.0 mm link-arm pivot bore so that it axially retains the front and rear link arms, while remaining clear of the rails and permitting the links to rotate and the sliding pivots to translate.
actions.unresolved_reference: The head diameter, axial thickness, edge treatment, and operating axial clearance are not specified. Select dimensions that provide positive retention without clamping the link arms; do not add heads to the short central pivot pins F021 and F022.
steps: Localize the four long members in the pivot pin assembly R04 using repeated-feature group G003: F017 lower right corner pivot pin, F018 lower left sliding pivot pin, F019 upper right fixed pivot pin, and F020 upper left sliding pivot pin. Exclude the short central pins F021 and F022 in group G004.
Use the existing cylindrical shaft faces FACE 30, FACE 38, FACE 121, and FACE 126 to recover each pin axis. All four axes are parallel to CAD Z, and each existing shaft has a radius of 2.4 mm.

Identify both exposed seating faces of every long pin: FACE 31 and FACE 33 for F017, FACE 39 and FACE 41 for F018, FACE 122 and FACE 124 for F019, and FACE 127 and FACE 129 for F020. The negative-Z ends are at CAD Z=-26.496377 mm and the positive-Z ends are at CAD Z=27.503623 mm.

Create a sketch on each negative-Z pin-end face. Project or reference the corresponding shaft circular edge, place a concentric circle on the recovered pin axis, and dimension it to the selected head diameter. Make the head diameter larger than the 5.0 mm link-arm bore diameter so the link eye cannot pass over the head.

Pad or extrude each negative-Z circular profile outward in the negative CAD Z direction by the selected head thickness. Fuse each extrusion only to its associated pin solid so that the pin and its head form one retained pin component; do not union the head with the rear link plates or either rail.

Repeat the concentric-circle sketch and outward extrusion on each positive-Z end face, extruding in the positive CAD Z direction. This creates a total of eight cylindrical retaining heads, with one head at each end of the four long corner pins.

Maintain a small functional axial clearance between the inner face of each new head and the adjacent outer link-arm face. The head must prevent axial escape without clamping the front or rear link plates and must preserve free rotation at all four corner pivots.

For sliding pivot pins F018 and F020, verify that the new heads move with the pin and do not contact the lower slot walls FACE 72, FACE 73, FACE 78, and FACE 80 or the upper slot walls FACE 111, FACE 112, FACE 117, and FACE 119 throughout the available CAD X travel.

If required by the design standard, apply a small equal chamfer or fillet to the outer circular edge of every head to remove sharp edges. Keep the inner retaining shoulder substantially square so that it continues to provide positive axial retention.

Pattern or copy the validated head construction across the four G003 pin axes, preserving coaxiality, equal head diameter, equal thickness, and symmetric placement at the positive-Z front and negative-Z back sides.

Recompute the assembly and confirm that the four long pins remain distinct from the rails and link solids, the fixed pivots still rotate, the slotted pivots still translate, and no link-arm bore can move axially past a new cylindrical head.

intention: Prevent the link arms from slipping off the long pins.
